10	
11	Verified 2026-07-31 against `origin/main` after I recommended "classify each event on
12	arrival" for org-scoped social feeds. **That recommendation was not buildable as stated.**
13	Three specific errors, each refuted by reading the code rather than the docs.
14	
15	## 1. There is NO inline classify-on-ingest path
16	
17	`packages/server/src/scheduled/classification-reconciliation.ts` opens with a doc comment
18	claiming classification is "normally triggered by: 1. Worker API (inline after content are
19	saved with embeddings) 2. Classifier enabled → runs inline 3. Classifier version updated →
20	runs inline", and calls itself a "FALLBACK"/"safety net".
21	
22	`git grep executeClassificationQuery origin/main` returns **exactly one caller** — the cron
23	job itself. `upsertClassifications` likewise has one caller, inside the same file. **The
24	inline paths the comment describes do not exist.** The "safety net" is the only net.
25	
26	Lesson: this file's own header is stale documentation. Applies the AGENTS.md rule —
27	absence is proven by `git grep … origin/main`, not by trusting a comment.
28	
29	## 2. Classifiers are CATEGORICAL + embedding-matched, not an LLM scorer
30	
31	`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-classifiers.ts:62` — `attribute_values` is a
32	`Type.Record(string, {description, examples[], embedding?})`: a MAP of value slug →
33	definition, with `min_similarity` (default 0.7) and `fallback_value`. Matching is cosine
34	similarity over embeddings (`classification-query.ts` — `cosineSimilarity`,
35	`determineBestMatches`), writing `source='embedding'`, `is_manual=false`.
36	
37	So a classifier yields **a label from a fixed set**, cheaply and with no LLM call. It
38	cannot produce a 0–100 score, a per-item `why`, or a drafted `suggested_action`. It is a
39	filter, not a writer. (`attribute_values` MUST be an object map, never an array — #2033.)
40	
41	## 3. Classification is ENTITY-scoped, so org-scoped feeds get NOTHING
42	
43	The reconciliation candidate query requires `e.entity_ids @> ARRAY[ent.id]` on an entity
44	whose `enabled_classifiers` is non-null, plus a row in `event_embeddings`. Entities that
45	*inherit* classifiers (`enabled_classifiers IS NULL`) are deliberately skipped — the
46	comment says the inline path covers them, and per (1) that path does not exist.
47	
48	Prod check on buremba: **100% of social events have no entity link** — X 1132/1132,
49	LinkedIn 67/67 over 7 days. `event_classifications` is **empty (0 rows)** org-wide. So
50	enabling a classifier on this feed today classifies exactly zero events.
51	
52	Classifier rows live in table `classify_facet` (not `classifiers`); `watcher_id IS NULL`
53	marks an org-level classifier, so they are not strictly Behavior-bound at the data layer
54	even though `classifiers.create` requires a `behavior_id`.
55	
56	## What this means for the "render on read" idea
57	
58	The direction survives — annotate once, render cheaply — but three gaps must close first:
59	org-scoped (not entity-scoped) classification, a real on-ingest trigger, and acceptance
60	that classifiers only filter. The buildable-today version needs no platform change: split
61	the cheap frequent filter from the expensive infrequent drafting, because runtime is
62	output-bound (see [[reference_behavior_prompt_bloat_and_zai_speed]]).
63

65	[[project_social_radar_voice_profile_health]].

Verified 2026-07-31 against `origin/main` after I recommended "classify each event on
arrival" for org-scoped social feeds. **That recommendation was not buildable as stated.**
Three specific errors, each refuted by reading the code rather than the docs.

## 1. There is NO inline classify-on-ingest path

`packages/server/src/scheduled/classification-reconciliation.ts` opens with a doc comment
claiming classification is "normally triggered by: 1. Worker API (inline after content are
saved with embeddings) 2. Classifier enabled → runs inline 3. Classifier version updated →
runs inline", and calls itself a "FALLBACK"/"safety net".

`git grep executeClassificationQuery origin/main` returns **exactly one caller** — the cron
job itself. `upsertClassifications` likewise has one caller, inside the same file. **The
inline paths the comment describes do not exist.** The "safety net" is the only net.

Lesson: this file's own header is stale documentation. Applies the AGENTS.md rule —
absence is proven by `git grep … origin/main`, not by trusting a comment.

## 2. Classifiers are CATEGORICAL + embedding-matched, not an LLM scorer

`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-classifiers.ts:62` — `attribute_values` is a
`Type.Record(string, {description, examples[], embedding?})`: a MAP of value slug →
definition, with `min_similarity` (default 0.7) and `fallback_value`. Matching is cosine
similarity over embeddings (`classification-query.ts` — `cosineSimilarity`,
`determineBestMatches`), writing `source='embedding'`, `is_manual=false`.

So a classifier yields **a label from a fixed set**, cheaply and with no LLM call. It
cannot produce a 0–100 score, a per-item `why`, or a drafted `suggested_action`. It is a
filter, not a writer. (`attribute_values` MUST be an object map, never an array — #2033.)

## 3. Classification is ENTITY-scoped, so org-scoped feeds get NOTHING

The reconciliation candidate query requires `e.entity_ids @> ARRAY[ent.id]` on an entity
whose `enabled_classifiers` is non-null, plus a row in `event_embeddings`. Entities that
*inherit* classifiers (`enabled_classifiers IS NULL`) are deliberately skipped — the
comment says the inline path covers them, and per (1) that path does not exist.

Prod check on buremba: **100% of social events have no entity link** — X 1132/1132,
LinkedIn 67/67 over 7 days. `event_classifications` is **empty (0 rows)** org-wide. So
enabling a classifier on this feed today classifies exactly zero events.

Classifier rows live in table `classify_facet` (not `classifiers`); `watcher_id IS NULL`
marks an org-level classifier, so they are not strictly Behavior-bound at the data layer
even though `classifiers.create` requires a `behavior_id`.

## What this means for the "render on read" idea

The direction survives — annotate once, render cheaply — but three gaps must close first:
org-scoped (not entity-scoped) classification, a real on-ingest trigger, and acceptance
that classifiers only filter. The buildable-today version needs no platform change: split
the cheap frequent filter from the expensive infrequent drafting, because runtime is
output-bound (see [[reference_behavior_prompt_bloat_and_zai_speed]]).

See [[project_classifier_collapse_and_keyed_promotion]],
[[project_social_radar_voice_profile_health]].

`is_manual=false`. A classifier yields **a label from a fixed set** — no score, no `why`.
(`attribute_values` MUST be an object map, never an array — #2033.)

## 3. The engine WORKS in prod — measured, correcting an earlier claim here

Read-only psql, 2026-07-31:

    classify_facet          28 total | 23 watcher_id IS NULL | 5 watcher-owned
    event_classifications   2189     | 2187 source='embedding' | 2 source='user'
    embedding rows written  2026-01-06 .. 2026-02-04   (nothing since — ~6 months)

    market   23 global, 13 active, 21 entity-scoped   <- owns all 2187 embedding rows
    buremba   0 global,  0 active,  5 watcher-owned   <- ALL `deprecated` e2e leftovers

**Earlier note in this file said `event_classifications` was empty org-wide. Wrong** — it
is empty for `buremba` only. The embedding path is proven end-to-end in production; it
simply has not run since 2026-02-04 and has never had a matchable classifier in `buremba`.

## 4. The trap: nothing you can CREATE is engine-matchable

`fetchClassifierTemplates` and both sibling lookups filter on all three
(`classification-query.ts` lines 234 / 330 / 490): `organization_id` (added by #2389 —
was a cross-org leak), `status='active'`, and **`watcher_id IS NULL`**.

Both write paths stamp `watcher_id`:
- `manage_classifiers create` → `handleCreate` looks up `WHERE id = ${behavior_id}` and
  inserts it as `watcher_id`. `behavior_id` is `Type.Optional` in the contract but the
  lookup fails without it ("Behavior not found: undefined"), so it is effectively REQUIRED.
- `watchers/classifier-extraction.ts:424` also inserts `${watcherId}`.

So every classifier created through the tool or ClientSDK is watcher-owned and invisible to
the engine forever. The 23 working `market` rows predate this and carry NULL. Short of
direct SQL there is no supported way to make a new matchable classifier. This — not the
entity-link gap alone — is why `buremba` has zero classifications.

The reconciliation candidate query requires `e.entity_ids @> ARRAY[ent.id]` on an entity
whose `enabled_classifiers` is non-null. Prod: **100% of buremba social events have no
entity link** (X 1132/1132, LinkedIn 67/67 over 7 days). `manage_classifiers apply`
(#2389) uses `mode: 'content_ids'` and needs no entity link — but it is **not exposed in
the agent SDK** (absent from `sandbox/namespaces/classifiers.ts` and `METHOD_METADATA`),
so only owner-admin MCP/REST callers can reach it.

## 6. Source precedence is real and designed

`event_classifications.source` is `embedding | llm | user`. `classify` writes llm/user with
`is_manual = true`; the engine's upsert deletes only `NOT is_manual`, so agent and human
judgment survives a bulk re-`apply`. `classify` has a batch mode, so an agent can read N
events, judge them, and store N verdicts with `reasoning` in one call.

See [[project_classifier_apply_verb_pr2389]], [[project_classifier_collapse_and_keyed_promotion]],
[[reference_behavior_prompt_bloat_and_zai_speed]], [[project_social_radar_voice_profile_health]].

content.text:
Yes — but I checked before answering, and the honest answer is "yes in design, no in practice." Here are the gaps, all verified against code and prod.

## First, a correction

I told you `event_classifications` was empty and the layer had never produced anything. That was wrong:

```
event_classifications   2189 rows | 2187 source='embedding' | 2 source='user'
written                 2026-01-06 .. 2026-02-04   (nothing since)

market    23 global classifiers, 13 active, 21 entity-scoped  ← owns all 2187
buremba    0 global,  0 active,  5 Behavior-owned, all deprecated
```

The embedding path is **proven end-to-end in production**. It just hasn't run since February, and has never had a matchable classifier in your org. That's a better fact than the one I gave you — it means the machinery works and the problem is reachability.

## The gaps

**Gap 1 — `apply` is invisible to agents.** I added it to the MCP tool but not to `sandbox/namespaces/classifiers.ts` or `METHOD_METADATA`. The agent SDK exposes `list`/`create`/`generateEmbeddings`/`delete`/`classify` and nothing else. So an agent literally cannot call the verb I just built. Only owner-admin MCP/REST callers (you, me via the Lobu MCP) can. That directly undercuts the claim you're asking me to confirm.

**Gap 2 — nothing an agent can create is engine-matchable.** This is the big one. The engine filters `watcher_id IS NULL` in all three lookup sites (`classification-query.ts:234/330/490`). But `create` does this:

```js
const watcher = await sql`SELECT id FROM watchers WHERE id = ${behaviorId} ...`;
if (watcher.length === 0) return { success: false, message: `Behavior not found: ${behaviorId}` };
// ...then inserts that id as watcher_id
```

`behavior_id` is `Type.Optional` in the contract, but the lookup fails without it, so it's effectively required. **Every classifier created through the tool or SDK is Behavior-owned, and therefore invisible to the engine forever.** Your 5 classifiers are all Behavior-owned. The 23 that work in `market` predate this and carry NULL. There is no supported way to create a matchable classifier short of direct SQL.

So today the honest version of my earlier answer is: an agent can create a classifier, and it will silently never match anything.

**Gap 3 — no measurement.** Still no way to know if a classifier is any good. Unchanged from what I said before.

**Gap 4 — `classify_facet_unique_per_insight` is `UNIQUE (entity_id, watcher_id, slug)`** with no `organization_id`. Global slugs are first-come-first-served across tenants.

**Gap 5 — the embedding cron hasn't written since Feb 4.** Six months. Either it stopped running or `market` ran out of candidates. Needs looking at, but not something I can fix blind.

## What holds up

The part of my answer that survives verification is the one that matters most for automation: `classify` accepts a **batch** of `{content_id, value, reasoning}` with `source='llm'`, writes `is_manual = true`, and the engine's bulk upsert deletes only `WHERE NOT is_manual`. So an agent reading 50 posts, judging them, and storing 50 verdicts with reasoning — that works today, is reachable from the SDK, and survives re-running `apply`. That's real ad-hoc classification.

What doesn't work today is the *cheap* half: define a bucket once, embed it, label thousands. Gaps 1 and 2 are what stand between you and that.

## Plan

Gaps 1 and 2 are one coherent concern — make the org-scoped classification path reachable by agents — and they're small: expose `apply` in the namespace + metadata, and let `behavior_id` be omitted so `create` can produce a global classifier. I'll do them as a follow-up PR off `main` once #2389 lands, since #2389 is reviewed clean and the follow-up depends on `apply` existing.

Gap 4 is a schema change, separate. Gap 5 is an investigation. Gap 3 is the agreement experiment, which becomes possible only after 1 and 2.

## PR #2389 status

```
pi-review   pass   bug_free 90, simplicity 82, slop 5, bugs 0, 0 blockers
typecheck   pass    unit  pass    frontend  pass    migrations  pass
integration pending
```

Waiting on `integration` in the background, then merging. I won't `--admin` past a check that hasn't reported.

## Confidence

- **Gap 1 and 2 are real — 95.** Read the namespace, the metadata table, the handler's watcher lookup, and all three engine filters; corroborated by prod showing your 5 classifiers Behavior-owned with zero classifications, and `market`'s 23 working ones all NULL.
- **The `classify` batch path works — 85.** Verified in code (batch mode, `is_manual=true`, upsert predicate). Not executed end-to-end; the 2 `user` rows in prod show the write path has been exercised at least once.
- **PR #2389 — 90.** Two independent clean reviews, full local suites, only `integration` outstanding.

Next: merge #2389, then the follow-up PR for gaps 1+2, then the agreement experiment as the real e2e.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

input.command:
git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(server): make the classification engine reachable by agents

Three defects that together made the embedding classifier unusable for anything
an agent or user could create.

1. `create` REQUIRED `behavior_id` and wrote it to `classify_facet.watcher_id`,
   while every engine lookup filters `cf.watcher_id IS NULL`. So every classifier
   creatable through the tool or the ClientSDK was invisible to the engine, and
   `apply`/the reconciliation cron reported clean zero-result runs over it.
   `behavior_id` is now optional; omit it for an org-level classifier.

2. `apply` was absent from the agent SDK namespace and METHOD_METADATA, so no
   agent could call the one verb that classifies without an entity link.

3. Fixing 1 exposed a crash 2 had been hiding: `classify_facet.entity_ids` and
   `current_event_records.entity_ids` are bigint[], which under fetch_types:false
   read back as the raw literal "{}" — not a JS array. "{}" is 2 chars, so the
   length guard passed and `.some` threw TypeError; the sibling read silently put
   the literal in a Set where no numeric membership test could match. Both now go
   through parsePgNumberArray.

Prod evidence for 1 (read-only, 2026-07-31): the org with working classifications
holds 23 classifiers, all watcher_id IS NULL and predating the required-behavior_id
rule; the org with none holds 5, all Behavior-owned.

Red: create-without-behavior_id rejected, then (after 1) TypeError
"classifierEntityIds.some is not a function", and namespace.apply undefined.
Green: 23/23 classifier integration, 23/23 method-metadata unit.
EOF
)" && git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD && git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD | tail -2

content.text:
#2389 merged (`eac0468da`). Then I addressed the gaps — and hit a third bug that the first two had been hiding.

## PR #2394 — three defects

**1. Nothing creatable was engine-matchable.** `create` required `behavior_id` and wrote it to `classify_facet.watcher_id`, while every engine lookup filters `watcher_id IS NULL`. Now optional: omit it for an org-level classifier.

**2. `apply` was invisible to agents.** Added to the SDK namespace and `METHOD_METADATA`.

**3. A crash the first two were hiding.** Once a created classifier could actually reach the engine, this appeared:

```
TypeError: classifierEntityIds.some is not a function
  at fetchClassifierTemplates (classification-query.ts:346:28)
```

`entity_ids` is `bigint[]`, which under `fetch_types:false` reads back as the raw literal `"{}"`, not an array. `"{}"` is 2 characters, so the `length > 0` guard passed and `.some` threw. I grepped the file and there was a second instance one function earlier — that one doesn't throw, it silently puts the literal into a `Set` where no numeric membership test can match. Both now go through `parsePgNumberArray`.

That second instance is the point: defect 1 made defect 3 unreachable, so it sat there looking fine. Neither was findable without the other fixed.

## The fixer pass earned its keep

`REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review-fix` works during the codex outage (memory said it was hard-wired to codex — that's been fixed). It caught two things I missed: a pinned `method-metadata` unit test asserting the old `behavior_id: string` signature, and `ClassifierCreateInput.behavior_id` still required in the SDK interface. It also corrected a factual error in my comment — `flatMap` doesn't split a string into characters; the Set just holds the raw literal.

## Evidence

Red, before:
```
× creates an engine-matchable classifier when no Behavior owns it
  → expected false to be true            (create rejected: behavior_id required)
× exposes apply on the agent SDK surface
  → expected 'undefined' to be 'function'
```
Green: 23/23 classifier integration, 23/23 method-metadata unit, `pre-pr` clean, typecheck 0.

Diff: 7 files, +272/−31. Review running on #2394.

## Answering your original question directly

Yes — agents can use ad-hoc classification to automate their work. But when you asked, that was only true for the LLM-judgment half (`classify`, batch, `is_manual=true`, survives re-`apply`). The cheap bulk half was broken in three independent ways, and none of them failed loudly: they produced successful, empty results. This PR is what makes the answer honest.

## Confidence

- **The three fixes are correct — 88.** Red→green on each, real pgvector, plus prod data corroborating defect 1's shape. Not yet run against a real classifier on real data.
- **Defect 3 is a class, and I got both instances — 80.** Grepped `entity_ids` across the engine file; both read sites are fixed. I have not swept other files for the same `bigint[]`-read pattern, which is the obvious next thing.

## Next

1. Merge #2394 when review and CI land.
2. **The e2e is now actually possible**: create a real classifier over your ~1400 embedded X/LinkedIn events, `apply` it, and run the agreement experiment against a 50-event LLM gold set. That gives you a number for whether embeddings are worth using on your data.
3. Sweep other files for the same raw-`bigint[]` read pattern.
4. `classify_facet` tenancy constraint — still open, needs a migration.

name: project_classifier_apply_verb_pr2389
description: "Classification made reachable: #2389 (apply verb + cross-org leak fix) and #2394 (four defects that made every creatable classifier a silent no-op), both MERGED. Corpus is 209k embedded events, not the 1.4k I first quoted — the scaling valve is needed NOW"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 13f0fe8f-d0cb-4f1a-b19c-1621ef6e6b2b
  modified: 2026-07-31T05:15:00.000Z
---

Two PRs, both MERGED 2026-07-31: **#2389** `eac0468da`, **#2394** `3ac8ba127`.
Prod-verify OWED for both (new MCP action + SDK method).

## #2389 — one verb, plus a real leak

`executeClassificationQuery` already supported `mode: 'content_ids'` (classify an
arbitrary id list, **no entity link required**) with integration coverage. Its only
caller, the reconciliation cron, hardcodes `mode: 'entity'`. Exposed it as
`manage_classifiers apply`.

**The leak:** `content_ids` mode filtered on `f.id IN (...)` only; the template lookup
on `cf.slug IN (...)` only. Neither org-scoped. RED: another org's event returned
`[{content_id: 3}]`, another org's same-slug classifier `[{content_id: 4}]`. GREEN: both
`[]`. Fix threads `organizationId` through `ClassificationQueryOptions` so the check sits
at the **engine** and the compiler forces every call site to supply it.

Also: re-running `apply` re-labels (`upsertClassifications` DELETEs
`NOT is_manual AND source='embedding'` then INSERTs). "Call it again" IS the invalidation.

## #2394 — four defects, every one of them silent

Follow-up after discovering `apply` could not be used with any classifier the API can create.

1. **`create` REQUIRED `behavior_id`** → written to `classify_facet.watcher_id`, while every
   engine lookup filters `watcher_id IS NULL`. Every classifier creatable through the tool
   or ClientSDK was invisible to the engine forever. Now optional.
2. **`apply` was absent from the agent SDK** (`sandbox/namespaces/classifiers.ts` +
   `METHOD_METADATA`), so no agent could call it.
3. **`handleList` filtered `fc.watcher_id IS NOT NULL`** → hid every org-level classifier
   from the agent that had just created one. create→list→apply broke at step 2.
4. **Raw `bigint[]` crash.** `entity_ids` under `fetch_types:false` reads back as the
   literal `"{}"` — 2 chars, so `length > 0` passed and `.some` threw TypeError. A sibling
   read put the literal into a `Set` where no numeric test could match. Both now go through
   `parsePgNumberArray`. Only reachable once (1) was fixed, because `create` writes
   `ARRAY[]::bigint[]` while prod's 13 working classifiers all have `entity_ids IS NULL`.

**The pattern worth remembering: every one of these failed as SILENCE** — a successful,
empty result. Not one threw where a user would see it. Three of the four were found only
because a test asserted a REASON rather than a count.

**Refuted hypothesis:** I theorised (4) had been killing the prod cron since its last write
on 2026-02-04. Checked — all 13 active prod classifiers have `entity_ids IS NULL`, which
short-circuits before `.some`. The cron is not crashing. **The Feb 4 stop is unexplained.**

## Corpus reality — corrects the "1400 events" figure

Measured 2026-07-31 (read-only psql), org `buremba`:

    total events   262,403      embedded (chunk 0)  209,097
    one model everywhere: Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5  (2,059,980 chunk-0 rows all orgs)
    no EMBEDDINGS_MODEL override in prod -> default matches stored rows, so `apply` WILL match

    (no connector_key)  54,552 events /  1,411 embedded   <- the one real coverage hole
    whatsapp.local      54,301 / 54,301      chrome.history 37,440 / 37,440
    chrome              30,535 / 30,535      spotify        23,563 / 23,505
    linkedin            10,263 / 10,263      twitter.takeout 8,292 /  8,292

**The 1,242 X + 175 LinkedIn figure was a 7-DAY WINDOW, not the corpus.** Embedding runs at
ingest and is already in Postgres. This invalidates the earlier advice that classification
"buys nothing today, it is a valve for later" — at 209k embedded events a Behavior cannot
prompt over the corpus, so the valve is needed NOW.

**New gap this exposes:** `apply` caps `content_ids` at 2000 per call, so the corpus is 105
calls. The bulk path was the cron, which is entity-scoped. There is no "classify everything"
verb.

## Still owed

- Prod-verify both PRs after rollout; entity-mode engine path is statically verified only.
- Sweep other files for the same raw `bigint[]` read pattern.
- `classify_facet_unique_per_insight` is `UNIQUE (entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` with **no
  organization_id** — global slugs are first-come-first-served across tenants.
- Why nothing has been classified since 2026-02-04.
- No way to measure classifier quality. Buildable from existing verbs: `classify` a ~50-event
  LLM gold set (`is_manual`, survives re-`apply`), `apply` embeddings over the same ids,
  `query_sql` the agreement rate.

## Gate notes

- A **Codesmith bot** auto-pushes fixes to your PR branch on CI failure (~3 min). Do NOT
  force-push over it — rebase. Both its commits on #2389 were correct.
- `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` AND `make review-fix` both work during the codex outage.
  The fixer earned its keep on #2394: it found defect (3), the pinned `method-metadata` test,
  and `ClassifierCreateInput.behavior_id` still required in the SDK interface.
- Pinned access matrix fails any new action missing from `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS` (silent fall
  to READ tier). Update the `ACCESS_SURFACE` fixture line too.

name: project_classifier_apply_verb_pr2389
description: "Classification made reachable: #2389 (apply verb + cross-org leak fix) and #2394 (four defects that made every creatable classifier a silent no-op), both MERGED. Corpus is 209k embedded events, not the 1.4k I first quoted — the scaling valve is needed NOW"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

Two PRs, both MERGED 2026-07-31: **#2389** `eac0468da`, **#2394** `3ac8ba127`.
Prod-verify OWED for both (new MCP action + SDK method).

## #2389 — one verb, plus a real leak

`executeClassificationQuery` already supported `mode: 'content_ids'` (classify an
arbitrary id list, **no entity link required**) with integration coverage. Its only
caller, the reconciliation cron, hardcodes `mode: 'entity'`. Exposed it as
`manage_classifiers apply`.

**The leak:** `content_ids` mode filtered on `f.id IN (...)` only; the template lookup
on `cf.slug IN (...)` only. Neither org-scoped. RED: another org's event returned
`[{content_id: 3}]`, another org's same-slug classifier `[{content_id: 4}]`. GREEN: both
`[]`. Fix threads `organizationId` through `ClassificationQueryOptions` so the check sits
at the **engine** and the compiler forces every call site to supply it.

Also: re-running `apply` re-labels (`upsertClassifications` DELETEs
`NOT is_manual AND source='embedding'` then INSERTs). "Call it again" IS the invalidation.

## #2394 — four defects, every one of them silent

Follow-up after discovering `apply` could not be used with any classifier the API can create.

1. **`create` REQUIRED `behavior_id`** → written to `classify_facet.watcher_id`, while every
   engine lookup filters `watcher_id IS NULL`. Every classifier creatable through the tool
   or ClientSDK was invisible to the engine forever. Now optional.
2. **`apply` was absent from the agent SDK** (`sandbox/namespaces/classifiers.ts` +
   `METHOD_METADATA`), so no agent could call it.
3. **`handleList` filtered `fc.watcher_id IS NOT NULL`** → hid every org-level classifier
   from the agent that had just created one. create→list→apply broke at step 2.
4. **Raw `bigint[]` crash.** `entity_ids` under `fetch_types:false` reads back as the
   literal `"{}"` — 2 chars, so `length > 0` passed and `.some` threw TypeError. A sibling
   read put the literal into a `Set` where no numeric test could match. Both now go through
   `parsePgNumberArray`. Only reachable once (1) was fixed, because `create` writes
   `ARRAY[]::bigint[]` while prod's 13 working classifiers all have `entity_ids IS NULL`.

**The pattern worth remembering: every one of these failed as SILENCE** — a successful,
empty result. Not one threw where a user would see it. Three of the four were found only
because a test asserted a REASON rather than a count.

**Refuted hypothesis:** I theorised (4) had been killing the prod cron since its last write
on 2026-02-04. Checked — all 13 active prod classifiers have `entity_ids IS NULL`, which
short-circuits before `.some`. The cron is not crashing. **The Feb 4 stop is unexplained.**

## Corpus reality — corrects the "1400 events" figure

Measured 2026-07-31 (read-only psql), org `buremba`:

    total events   262,403      embedded (chunk 0)  209,097
    one model everywhere: Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5  (2,059,980 chunk-0 rows all orgs)
    no EMBEDDINGS_MODEL override in prod -> default matches stored rows, so `apply` WILL match

    (no connector_key)  54,552 events /  1,411 embedded   <- the one real coverage hole
    whatsapp.local      54,301 / 54,301      chrome.history 37,440 / 37,440
    chrome              30,535 / 30,535      spotify        23,563 / 23,505
    linkedin            10,263 / 10,263      twitter.takeout 8,292 /  8,292

**The 1,242 X + 175 LinkedIn figure was a 7-DAY WINDOW, not the corpus.** Embedding runs at
ingest and is already in Postgres. This invalidates the earlier advice that classification
"buys nothing today, it is a valve for later" — at 209k embedded events a Behavior cannot
prompt over the corpus, so the valve is needed NOW.

**New gap this exposes:** `apply` caps `content_ids` at 2000 per call, so the corpus is 105
calls. The bulk path was the cron, which is entity-scoped. There is no "classify everything"
verb.

## Still owed

- Prod-verify both PRs after rollout; entity-mode engine path is statically verified only.
- Sweep other files for the same raw `bigint[]` read pattern.
- `classify_facet_unique_per_insight` is `UNIQUE (entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` with **no
  organization_id** — global slugs are first-come-first-served across tenants.
- Why nothing has been classified since 2026-02-04.
- No way to measure classifier quality. Buildable from existing verbs: `classify` a ~50-event
  LLM gold set (`is_manual`, survives re-`apply`), `apply` embeddings over the same ids,
  `query_sql` the agreement rate.

- A **Codesmith bot** auto-pushes fixes to your PR branch on CI failure (~3 min). Do NOT
  force-push over it — rebase. Both its commits on #2389 were correct.
- `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` AND `make review-fix` both work during the codex outage.
  The fixer earned its keep on #2394: it found defect (3), the pinned `method-metadata` test,
  and `ClassifierCreateInput.behavior_id` still required in the SDK interface.
- Pinned access matrix fails any new action missing from `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS` (silent fall
  to READ tier). Update the `ACCESS_SURFACE` fixture line too.
- Integration tests: `env -u DATABASE_URL` for ephemeral embedded pg. `cleanupTestDatabase()`
  TRUNCATEs everything — never point it at prod.
- Fresh worktree needs `make build-packages`; editing a `packages/core` contract needs
  `tsc --build --force packages/core/tsconfig.json` ([[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]]).

Corrects [[reference_classifier_layer_is_entity_scoped_and_cron_only]].
See [[reference_behavior_prompt_bloat_and_zai_speed]], [[reference_fetch_types_false_raw_array]].

name: project_classifier_apply_verb_pr2389
description: "PR #2389 — the classification engine's content_ids mode was built+tested but unreachable; exposing it as manage_classifiers apply surfaced a real cross-org leak (proven red->green). Also: a Codesmith bot auto-pushes fixes to your branch on CI failure"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 13f0fe8f-d0cb-4f1a-b19c-1621ef6e6b2b
  modified: 2026-07-31T02:43:18.713Z
---

Built 2026-07-31 in worktree `.claude/worktrees/classifier-apply-verb`, branch
`feat/classifier-apply-verb`, PR #2389.

## What was actually missing (one verb, not a subsystem)

`executeClassificationQuery` already supported `mode: 'content_ids'` — classify an
arbitrary id list, **no entity link required**, `WHERE f.id IN (...) AND fe.embedding IS
NOT NULL` — and had integration coverage. The only production caller (the reconciliation
cron) hardcodes `mode: 'entity'`, whose candidate query needs `e.entity_ids @> ARRAY[ent.id]`.
Prod: 100% of X/LinkedIn events have no entity link, so no org-scoped feed could ever be
classified. `event_classifications` was empty org-wide.

Everything else I first claimed was needed was wrong:
- **No versioning needed.** `upsertClassifications` DELETEs `NOT is_manual AND
  source='embedding'` then INSERTs, so re-running re-labels. Edit classifier →
  `generate_embeddings` → `apply` again. "Call it again" IS the invalidation.
- **Embedding coverage was fine** — X 1242/1242, LinkedIn 175/175 embedded.

## The real find: cross-org leak, proven

`content_ids` mode filtered on `f.id IN (...)` only; the template lookup on
`cf.slug IN (...)` only. Neither scoped by org. Unreachable from a trusted cron; a live
tenant-isolation bug the moment an agent passes ids. RED (filters reverted):
`expected [{content_id: 3}] to deeply equal []` for another org's event, and
`[{content_id: 4}]` for another org's same-slug classifier. GREEN after: both `[]`.

Fix threads `organizationId` through `ClassificationQueryOptions` so the check sits at the
**engine**, not per caller — the compiler then forces every call site to supply it.

## ⚠️ A Codesmith bot auto-pushes fixes to your PR branch

Twice during this PR, commits appeared on my branch authored `buremba` +
`Co-authored-by: Codesmith <codesmith-bot@users.noreply.github.com>`, reacting to CI
failures within ~3 minutes. `git push` then fails with the fast-forward hint and
`git status -sb` shows `[ahead 1, behind 1]`.

**Do not force-push over it — rebase.** Both of its commits were correct, and the second
found two genuine bugs in my handler that I had missed:
1. My `has_embedding` pre-check ignored `embedding_model`, and my template lookup omitted
   `watcher_id IS NULL`, so they diverged from the engine's own filters — a watcher-owned
   classifier or stale-model chunk-0 vector read as "found/embedded" and its zero results
   got misblamed on `below_threshold`. Exactly the misreporting the feature exists to stop.
2. `handleApply` could throw out of `routeAction` instead of returning `success:false`
   like `classify`.

Lesson: **any pre-check that explains a downstream engine's results must mirror that
engine's filters exactly**, or the explanation is worse than none.

## Gate notes

- The **pinned access matrix** (`auth/__tests__/tool-access.test.ts`) fails any newly
  registered action missing from `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS` — it silently falls to READ tier.
  Adding an agent-facing action means updating `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS` + the `ACCESS_SURFACE`
  fixture line. Caught this in CI, not locally, because I ran the integration file first.
- `make review-fix` and `make review` BOTH dead: codex over quota until Aug 5th 2026.
  `pi-review` is a REQUIRED check, so the PR is BLOCKED on it regardless of green CI.
  See [[project_review_harness_codex_single_point]].
- Integration tests: run with `env -u DATABASE_URL` so global setup spawns ephemeral
  embedded Postgres. **`cleanupTestDatabase()` TRUNCATEs every table — never point it at
  prod.** Prod `DATABASE_URL` is commented out in `.env` (extract from the comment for
  read-only psql).
- A fresh worktree needs `make build-packages` before vitest, or you get a cascade of
  `Cannot find package '@lobu/connector-sdk/...'` / `@lobu/connector-worker/compile`.
  Editing a `packages/core` contract also needs core rebuilt or server typecheck shows
  dozens of phantom errors in untouched files ([[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]]).

## Design context

Classification is a **scaling valve, not a pipeline stage** — see
[[reference_behavior_prompt_bloat_and_zai_speed]]. Behavior runtime is output-bound: a 59%
prompt cut (325 KB → 132 KB) left runtime unchanged. So this buys nothing until a candidate
set is too big to pass at all; it adds the escape hatch without touching the hot path.
Corrects [[reference_classifier_layer_is_entity_scoped_and_cron_only]], which said the
org-scoped path did not exist — the ENGINE had it; only the agent-facing verb was missing.

Under the limit (17,041 bytes, was 20.3KB), every file still reachable by link or grep line.

## Answering you directly: yes, embedding already runs at ingest

You were right and my number was wrong. `buremba` holds **262,403 events, 209,097 embedded** — one model everywhere, `Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5`, 2.06M chunk-0 rows across all orgs. The 1,242 X + 175 LinkedIn figure I kept quoting was a **7-day window**, and I repeated it as if it were the corpus.

Coverage is near-total per source:

| source | events | embedded |
|---|---|---|
| (no connector_key) | 54,552 | **1,411** |
| whatsapp.local | 54,301 | 54,301 |
| chrome.history | 37,440 | 37,440 |
| chrome | 30,535 | 30,535 |
| spotify | 23,563 | 23,505 |
| linkedin | 10,263 | 10,263 |
| twitter.takeout | 8,292 | 8,292 |

One real hole: 53k events with no `connector_key` are unembedded.

I also checked the thing that would have made all this moot — prod has no `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` override, so the configured default matches every stored row exactly. `apply` will find these embeddings.

## This invalidates advice I gave you earlier

I said classification "buys nothing today — it's a valve for later, install it before you need it." That was reasoned from 1,400 events. At **209,097 embedded events** the valve is needed *now*: no Behavior can prompt over that corpus, so filtering before the prompt isn't optimization, it's the only way to query it at all.

**And it exposes a new gap I should flag rather than bury:** `apply` caps `content_ids` at 2,000 per call. Your corpus is 105 calls. The bulk path was always the cron, which is entity-scoped and hasn't written since February. So there is still no "classify everything" verb — only "classify these 2,000."

## Merged

**#2394** `3ac8ba127` — all required checks green, `pi-review` 88/85/5, 0 blockers, 0 suggested fixes. Four defects fixed. Both PRs now in `main`.

Memory updated with the corpus numbers, the four defects, the refuted Feb-4 hypothesis, and the corrected scaling advice.

## Confidence

- **Corpus numbers — 95.** Direct read-only queries against prod, just now.
- **`apply` will match in prod — 90.** Model stamp verified against config and against all 2.06M rows; no override in any prod deployment.
- **The 2,000-cap gap — 90.** Read off the contract; arithmetic against the measured corpus.

## Next

1. **Prod-verify both PRs** after Flux rollout (~30–60 min). Per your own recipe: gate on per-pod image, not `/health`, and on the squash SHAs `eac0468da` / `3ac8ba127`.
2. **The e2e is now worth much more than I thought** — a real classifier over 209k embedded events, not 1.4k.
3. **Decide on the bulk gap**: raise the 2,000 cap, add a filter-based `apply` (classify everything matching a predicate), or accept 105 paged calls.
4. The 53k unembedded no-`connector_key` events — worth understanding what they are.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   Seven user requests in this session, building on prior work:
   1. "do the flagged thing. also how confident are you that we're good to go? can we skip 1 and do 2 and explain 3" — implement the skip-reason fixture test I'd flagged; give confidence; skip re-running review (item 1), do the e2e (item 2), explain the Behavior 71 output-shape fix (item 3).
   2. "is this a hack or a solution?" — a design challenge on the precheck approach.
   3. "what's that slice etc" — asking what `slice(0, 20)` / the sample arrays were for.
   4. "why do we need those? is it overengineered" — challenge on whether the skip-reason apparatus was justified.
   5. "is this architecture best or could we just give the agent postgresql sql access and it can do everthing? go through usecases how it's useful and why and let's guide me" — architecture guidance request.
   6. "so you say agents can use adhoc classifications to automate their job right?" followed mid-turn by "identify all the gaps and address them" — verify the claim and fix everything blocking it.
   7. "why only 1400, don't we do the embedification already and insert to postgresql" — challenge to my corpus-size figure.

   Through-line: make the classification subsystem genuinely usable by agents, simplify rather than complicate, and verify claims empirically rather than asserting them.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Lobu platform**: Bun workspace monorepo; packages `core`/`server`/`agent-worker`/`connectors`/`plugin-api`/`plugin-host`/`owletto`
   - **Behaviors** (agent-facing name; `watcher` is internal DB vocabulary — must not appear on exposed surfaces; `make pre-pr` fails on it)
   - **Classification engine**: `executeClassificationQuery` with `mode: 'entity' | 'content_ids'`; categorical labels via embedding cosine similarity over `classify_facet.attribute_values`; `min_similarity` + `fallback_value`
   - **Three engine target conjuncts**: `organization_id`, `status='active'`, `watcher_id IS NULL` (lines 234/330/490 of `classification-query.ts`)
   - **`event_classifications.source`**: `embedding | llm | user`; `classify` writes `is_manual=true`; engine upsert deletes only `WHERE NOT is_manual` — so agent/human judgment survives bulk re-`apply`
   - **`current_event_records`** = `SELECT ... FROM events WHERE superseded_by IS NULL`
   - **`fetch_types:false` raw-array trap**: `bigint[]`/`text[]` columns read back as raw literals (`"{}"`, `"{1,2}"`, `"{positive}"`), not JS arrays; helpers `parsePgNumberArray`, `parsePgTextArray`, `pgBigintArray`, `pgTextArray` in `db/client.ts`
   - **Access tiers**: `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS` / `MEMBER_WRITE_ACTIONS` / `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS`; pinned `ACCESS_SURFACE` fixture; a new action missing from `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS` silently falls to READ tier
   - **MCP scopes**: `mcp:read`/`mcp:write`/`mcp:admin`; `hasRequiredMcpScope` fails closed on null/empty
   - **`query_sql`**: runs inside `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`; `event_classifications` is exposed via `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA` (`table-schema.ts:472`)
   - **TypeBox contracts** in `packages/core/src/contracts/tools/`
   - **Review harness**: `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` and `make review-fix` both work during the codex quota outage (codex returns Aug 5); `CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL` defaults to `fable`

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **PR #2389 (merged `eac0468da`), worktree `classifier-apply-verb`:**

   - **`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_classifiers.ts`** — the `apply` handler. Final shape after simplification:
     ```ts
     type SkipReason = 'not_in_organization' | 'superseded' | 'not_embedded' | 'below_threshold';

     const SKIP_REASON_TEXT: Record<SkipReason, string> = {
       not_in_organization: 'not in this organization',
       superseded: 'superseded',
       not_embedded: 'not embedded',
       below_threshold: 'below min_similarity',
     };
     ```
     The precheck query (reads `events`, NOT the view, so liveness is separable):
     ```ts
     const inOrg = (await sql`
       SELECT e.id,
              (e.superseded_by IS NULL) AS is_live,
              EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM event_embeddings emb
                WHERE emb.event_id = e.id
                  AND emb.chunk_index = 0
                  AND emb.embedding_model = ${getConfiguredEmbeddingModel()}
              ) AS has_embedding
       FROM events e
       WHERE e.organization_id = ${ctx.organizationId}
         AND e.id = ANY(${pgBigintArray(requestedIds)}::bigint[])
     `) as unknown as Array<{ id: number; is_live: boolean; has_embedding: boolean }>;
     ```
     The single ordered pass replacing 4 parallel filters + 3 sample arrays:
     ```ts
     const skipped: Array<{ id: number; reason: SkipReason }> = [];
     for (const id of requestedIds) {
       const row = byId.get(id);
       if (!row) skipped.push({ id, reason: 'not_in_organization' });
       else if (!row.is_live) skipped.push({ id, reason: 'superseded' });
       else if (!row.has_embedding) skipped.push({ id, reason: 'not_embedded' });
       else if (!classified.has(id)) skipped.push({ id, reason: 'below_threshold' });
     }
     const counts: Record<SkipReason, number> = { not_in_organization: 0, superseded: 0, not_embedded: 0, below_threshold: 0 };
     for (const s of skipped) counts[s.reason]++;
     ```
     Returns `data: { requested, classified, skipped: counts, sample_skipped: skipped.slice(0, 20) }`.

   - **`packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/classifiers/classifiers-apply-skip-reasons.test.ts`** (NEW, ~286 lines) — pins each skip reason. One `apply` call over 7 ids: classifiable (basis 0), orthogonal (basis 7 → below_threshold), unembedded, staleModel (`embedding: basisVector(0)`, `embedding_model: 'legacy-embedding-model-v0'`), superseded, foreign org, and `unknownId = 999_999_999`. Asserts exact id→reason pairing. Supersession done as production does:
     ```ts
     await sql`UPDATE events SET supersedes_event_id = ${superseded.id} WHERE id = ${replacement.id}`;
     await sql`UPDATE events SET superseded_by = ${replacement.id} WHERE id = ${superseded.id}`;
     ```
     Requires `scopes: ['mcp:admin']` in the ToolContext (apply is owner-admin tier). Includes a fixture guard asserting `staleModel` actually has a vector with the legacy stamp.

   **PR #2394 (merged `3ac8ba127`), worktree `classifier-agent-reachable`:**

   - **`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_classifiers.ts`** — `handleCreate` made `behavior_id` optional:
     ```ts
     const entityId = args.entity_id ?? null;
     // Optional on purpose. `behavior_id` becomes `classify_facet.watcher_id`, and
     // every embedding-engine lookup filters `cf.watcher_id IS NULL` — so while
     // this was required, EVERY classifier creatable through this tool or the
     // ClientSDK was invisible to the engine...
     const behaviorId = args.behavior_id ?? null;
     if (behaviorId !== null) { /* watcher lookup, else "Behavior not found" */ }
     ```
     `handleList` conditions changed from `['fc.watcher_id IS NOT NULL', 'fc.organization_id = $1']` to `['fc.organization_id = $1']` (fixer's catch).

   - **`packages/server/src/utils/classification-query.ts`** — two raw-array reads fixed:
     ```ts
     import { type DbClient, getDb, parsePgNumberArray, pgTextArray } from '../db/client';
     // in fetchTargetContent:
     entity_ids: parsePgNumberArray(row.entity_ids),
     // in fetchClassifierTemplates:
     const classifierEntityIds = parsePgNumberArray(row.entity_ids ?? []);
     ```

   - **`packages/server/src/sandbox/namespaces/classifiers.ts`** — added `ClassifierApplyInput`, `apply(input): Promise<unknown>` to the interface, `apply: (input) => action("apply", input)` to the impl, and made `ClassifierCreateInput.behavior_id` optional.

   - **`packages/server/src/sandbox/method-metadata.ts`** — added `"classifiers.apply"` with `access: "admin"`, `cost: "expensive"`; rewrote `classifiers.create` summary/signature/example to drop the "REQUIRES behavior_id" framing.

   - **`packages/server/src/__tests__/unit/sandbox/method-metadata.test.ts`** — pinned fragment `"behavior_id: string"` → `"behavior_id?: string"` (fixer's catch).

   - **`packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/classifiers/classifiers-agent-reachable.test.ts`** (NEW) — 3 tests: create-without-behavior_id → `watcher_id` NULL → list shows it → apply classifies it (writes `source='embedding'`, `values=['positive']`); create-with-behavior_id still works and stays outside the engine; SDK surface exposes `apply` with `access: 'admin'`.

   - **`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-classifiers.ts`** — `behavior_id` description rewritten to say OMIT for org-level.

4. **Errors and fixes:**

   - **Superseded event mislabeled `not_in_organization`** — found while writing the test; reading through `current_event_records` collapsed liveness and org membership. Fixed by reading `events` + deriving `is_live`.
   - **Over-engineered result shape** — user challenged ("why do we need those? is it overengineered"). Collapsed 7 potentially-disagreeing fields into one derived list.
   - **Mutation B survived (dropping `embedding_model` filter did not fail the test)** — root cause was a fixture bug I introduced: a python sed replacement dropped the `embedding: basisVector(0)` line from `staleModel`, so it degraded into a duplicate of `unembedded`. Two PRs, both MERGED 2026-07-31: **#2389** `eac0468da`, **#2394** `3ac8ba127`.
Prod-verify OWED for both (new MCP action + SDK method).

## #2389 — one verb, plus a real leak

`executeClassificationQuery` already supported `mode: 'content_ids'` (classify an
arbitrary id list, **no entity link required**) with integration coverage. Its only
caller, the reconciliation cron, hardcodes `mode: 'entity'`. Exposed it as
`manage_classifiers apply`.

**The leak:** `content_ids` mode filtered on `f.id IN (...)` only; the template lookup
on `cf.slug IN (...)` only. Neither org-scoped. RED: another org's event returned
`[{content_id: 3}]`, another org's same-slug classifier `[{content_id: 4}]`. GREEN: both
`[]`. Fix threads `organizationId` through `ClassificationQueryOptions` so the check sits
at the **engine** and the compiler forces every call site to supply it.

Also: re-running `apply` re-labels (`upsertClassifications` DELETEs
`NOT is_manual AND source='embedding'` then INSERTs). "Call it again" IS the invalidation.

## #2394 — four defects, every one of them silent

Follow-up after discovering `apply` could not be used with any classifier the API can create.

1. **`create` REQUIRED `behavior_id`** → written to `classify_facet.watcher_id`, while every
   engine lookup filters `watcher_id IS NULL`. Every classifier creatable through the tool
   or ClientSDK was invisible to the engine forever. Now optional.
2. **`apply` was absent from the agent SDK** (`sandbox/namespaces/classifiers.ts` +
   `METHOD_METADATA`), so no agent could call it.
3. **`handleList` filtered `fc.watcher_id IS NOT NULL`** → hid every org-level classifier
   from the agent that had just created one. create→list→apply broke at step 2.
4. **Raw `bigint[]` crash.** `entity_ids` under `fetch_types:false` reads back as the
   literal `"{}"` — 2 chars, so `length > 0` passed and `.some` threw TypeError. A sibling
   read put the literal into a `Set` where no numeric test could match. Both now go through
   `parsePgNumberArray`. Only reachable once (1) was fixed, because `create` writes
   `ARRAY[]::bigint[]` while prod's 13 working classifiers all have `entity_ids IS NULL`.

**The pattern worth remembering: every one of these failed as SILENCE** — a successful,
empty result. Not one threw where a user would see it. Three of the four were found only
because a test asserted a REASON rather than a count.

**Refuted hypothesis:** I theorised (4) had been killing the prod cron since its last write
on 2026-02-04. Checked — all 13 active prod classifiers have `entity_ids IS NULL`, which
short-circuits before `.some`. The cron is not crashing. **The Feb 4 stop is unexplained.**

## Corpus reality — corrects the "1400 events" figure

Measured 2026-07-31 (read-only psql), org `buremba`:

    total events   262,403      embedded (chunk 0)  209,097
    one model everywhere: Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5  (2,059,980 chunk-0 rows all orgs)
    no EMBEDDINGS_MODEL override in prod -> default matches stored rows, so `apply` WILL match

    (no connector_key)  54,552 events /  1,411 embedded   <- the one real coverage hole
    whatsapp.local      54,301 / 54,301      chrome.history 37,440 / 37,440
    chrome              30,535 / 30,535      spotify        23,563 / 23,505
    linkedin            10,263 / 10,263      twitter.takeout 8,292 /  8,292

**The 1,242 X + 175 LinkedIn figure was a 7-DAY WINDOW, not the corpus.** Embedding runs at
ingest and is already in Postgres. This invalidates the earlier advice that classification
"buys nothing today, it is a valve for later" — at 209k embedded events a Behavior cannot
prompt over the corpus, so the valve is needed NOW.

**New gap this exposes:** `apply` caps `content_ids` at 2000 per call, so the corpus is 105
calls. The bulk path was the cron, which is entity-scoped. There is no "classify everything"
verb.

## Still owed

- Prod-verify both PRs after rollout; entity-mode engine path is statically verified only.
- Sweep other files for the same raw `bigint[]` read pattern.
- `classify_facet_unique_per_insight` is `UNIQUE (entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` with **no
  organization_id** — global slugs are first-come-first-served across tenants.
- Why nothing has been classified since 2026-02-04.
- No way to measure classifier quality. Buildable from existing verbs: `classify` a ~50-event
  LLM gold set (`is_manual`, survives re-`apply`), `apply` embeddings over the same ids,
  `query_sql` the agreement rate.

## Gate notes

- A **Codesmith bot** auto-pushes fixes to your PR branch on CI failure (~3 min). Do NOT
  force-push over it — rebase. Both its commits on #2389 were correct.
- `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` AND `make review-fix` both work during the codex outage.
  The fixer earned its keep on #2394: it found defect (3), the pinned `method-metadata` test,
  and `ClassifierCreateInput.behavior_id` still required in the SDK interface.
- Pinned access matrix fails any new action missing from `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS` (silent fall
  to READ tier). Update the `ACCESS_SURFACE` fixture line too.
- Integration tests: `env -u DATABASE_URL` for ephemeral embedded pg. `cleanupTestDatabase()`
  TRUNCATEs everything — never point it at prod.
- Fresh worktree needs `make build-packages`; editing a `packages/core` contract needs
  `tsc --build --force packages/core/tsconfig.json` ([[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]]).

Corrects [[reference_classifier_layer_is_entity_scoped_and_cron_only]].
See [[reference_behavior_prompt_bloat_and_zai_speed]], [[reference_fetch_types_false_raw_array]].

aiTitle: Check lobu setup for X and LinkedIn timeline

content.text:
Both PRs are verified live, and the verification turned up a fifth defect of the same family.

## Deployment gate

`app.lobu.ai/health` reports revision `bae1e0f11`, all four prod pods on image `20260731-065012-001790`. Both squash commits are ancestors:

```
eac0468da (#2389) DEPLOYED
3ac8ba127 (#2394) DEPLOYED
```

## What works in prod

I ran the whole chain against the real `buremba` corpus, not a fixture.

`search_sdk` returns `classifiers.apply` with the skip-reason contract, and `classifiers.create` carries the corrected "OMIT `behavior_id`" guidance. Then:

- **create without `behavior_id`** → `classifier_id: 201`, `watcher_id NULL`, 3 attribute embeddings auto-generated. This exact call was rejected before #2394.
- **list** → returns it with `behavior_id: null`. Under the old `watcher_id IS NOT NULL` filter this was empty.
- **apply over 500 real x/twitter events + one bogus id**:

```
Classified 280/501; 1 not in this organization; 220 below min_similarity
skipped: {not_in_organization: 1, superseded: 0, not_embedded: 0, below_threshold: 220}
```

**`not_embedded: 0` across 500 real prod events** is the number I most wanted — it confirms the configured model stamp matches what's actually stored, which was my largest untested assumption. And the bogus id came back named rather than silently dropped.

The labels are genuinely right, not just present: `congrats to my friends at zellic` / `Thank you @marcklingen for all the support` → positive; `Claude's system prompt is a disaster` / `blank out rejecting LLM-based code` → negative. One honest miss — a Turkish post meaning "seeing work like this makes me love Three.js even more" was labeled negative. The English embedding model is weak cross-lingually, which matters given roughly half this corpus is Turkish.

## The new defect

`apply` reported 280 written. `query_sql` on `event_classifications` returned **0**. The rows are real — direct psql found 282 for this org — but the read path can't see them.

`execute-data-sources.ts:629` scopes `event_classifications` through entities only:

```sql
JOIN public.entities ent ON ent.id = ANY(ev.entity_ids)
WHERE ev.id = ec.event_id AND ent.organization_id = $org
```

The sibling `events` CTE 88 lines earlier uses a three-way OR — `ev.organization_id` **OR** entity **OR** connection. The classifications CTE implements only the middle disjunct, and its own comment says it means to mirror `events`.

So every classification on an event with no entity link is invisible. That is precisely what `apply` is *for* — its own docs say "Needs no entity link, so this is how org-scoped feed content gets classified." 281 of my 282 rows have no entity link. Measured both predicates against prod:

```
current CTE predicate:      0
events-style predicate:   280   <- exactly what apply reported
```

Same failure class as the four in #2394: a successful, empty, silent result. An agent would classify 209k events and then find nothing when it queried them back.

## Confidence

- **Both PRs live and working — 96.** Full create→list→apply chain against the prod corpus, labels inspected by hand.
- **The read-path defect — 95.** Confirmed on `origin/main`, and the corrected predicate reproduces `apply`'s exact count.
- **Classifier quality — 70.** Eyeballed ~14 of 280; no gold set. Cross-lingual weakness is real but unquantified.

## Next

1. **Fix the CTE** — mirror the `events` three-way scope. One-line class of change, but a new concern so it wants its own branch. Say the word and I'll open it.
2. I left classifier 201 and its 280 rows in prod — correct, useful data, and deleting is the destructive direction. Tell me if you'd rather I deprecate it.
3. **Cross-lingual gap** is worth a decision: a Turkish-capable embedding model, or per-language classifiers.
4. The 2,000-id cap still stands — 209k events is 105 calls with no bulk verb.

content.content: @AGENTS.md
content.rawContent:
<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."

10	
11	On 2026-07-28 a concurrent agent/automation on this machine twice destroyed in-flight work in `.claude/worktrees/`: first it deleted the whole `activity-memory-split` worktree (uncommitted owletto changes lost, reconstructed from conversation context), later it gutted the recreated worktree down to `packages/owletto` and de-registered it (`git worktree list` no longer showed it; git commands inside fell through to the MAIN checkout — which it left sitting on a feature branch). Disk was also at 99% with the automation re-installing node_modules in worktrees as fast as caches were cleared.
12	
13	**Why:** worktrees are shared mutable state between sessions; a cleanup/bump job prunes what looks stale, and uncommitted submodule changes don't make the outer worktree look dirty.
14	
15	**How to apply:**
16	- In a submodule worktree, `git commit` + `git push -u origin <branch>` as soon as a coherent chunk exists — BEFORE running long gates. Pushed commits survived both wipes; working trees did not.
