1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.

-- migrate:up

-- Stamp every existing classifier label vector with the model that produced it.
--
-- `classify_facet.attribute_values[value].embedding` is cosine-compared against
-- `event_embeddings.embedding`. The event side has been model-scoped since
-- 20260526120000 (stamp) / 20260618140000 (NOT NULL, part of the PK), because
-- vectors from different models are not comparable even at equal dimensionality.
-- The label side never got a stamp, so it is the half a model swap leaves
-- behind — and cosine over two incompatible 768-dim spaces returns a plausible
-- number rather than an error, so classification keeps running and silently
-- assigns wrong labels.
--
-- The engine now drops any label vector whose stamp is not the configured model.
-- Without this backfill that guard would treat all 208 existing vectors
-- (28 classifiers, measured on prod 2026-07-31) as unknown-provenance and stop
-- classifying at deploy — so this migration is what makes the guard a no-op for
-- data that is in fact fine.
--
-- The stamp is DERIVED, not hardcoded: label vectors were produced by whatever
-- model the install has been running, so read that off event_embeddings rather
-- than assuming the default. Prod holds exactly one distinct value
-- (Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5, 2,060,864 rows), and an install with no events at
-- all falls back to the code default. The aggregate is a one-time full scan of a
-- ~2M-row table in the deploy hook (seconds); it is the "run the aggregation in
-- a migration, never per request" case, and nothing reads it again afterwards.
--
-- Idempotent: only entries with a vector AND no stamp are touched, so a re-run
-- is a no-op. Deliberately does NOT invent a stamp for entries with no vector —
-- a stamp must never outlive the vector it describes.

WITH prevailing AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(
        (SELECT embedding_model
           FROM public.event_embeddings
          GROUP BY embedding_model
          ORDER BY count(*) DESC
          LIMIT 1),
        'Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5'
    ) AS model
)
UPDATE public.classify_facet cf
SET attribute_values = (
        SELECT jsonb_object_agg(
            e.key,
            CASE
                WHEN jsonb_typeof(e.value) = 'object'
                 AND jsonb_typeof(e.value -> 'embedding') = 'array'
                 AND NOT (e.value ? 'embedding_model')
                THEN e.value || jsonb_build_object('embedding_model', (SELECT model FROM prevailing))
                ELSE e.value
            END
        )
          FROM jsonb_each(cf.attribute_values) e
    ),
    updated_at = now()
WHERE jsonb_typeof(cf.attribute_values) = 'object'
  -- Guards the jsonb_object_agg above: over zero rows it returns NULL, which
  -- would blank the column. An entry-less `{}` cannot reach the SET.
  AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
          FROM jsonb_each(cf.attribute_values) e
         WHERE jsonb_typeof(e.value) = 'object'
           AND jsonb_typeof(e.value -> 'embedding') = 'array'
           AND NOT (e.value ? 'embedding_model')
    );

-- migrate:down

-- Strip the stamp back out. Vectors are left in place — they were never
-- rewritten, only annotated.
UPDATE public.classify_facet cf
SET attribute_values = (
        SELECT jsonb_object_agg(
            e.key,
            CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(e.value) = 'object'
                 THEN e.value - 'embedding_model'
                 ELSE e.value END
        )
          FROM jsonb_each(cf.attribute_values) e
    )
WHERE jsonb_typeof(cf.attribute_values) = 'object'
  AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_each(cf.attribute_values) e
         WHERE jsonb_typeof(e.value) = 'object' AND e.value ? 'embedding_model'
    );

git push -q -u origin feat/cf-org-unique 2>&1 | tail -3; gh pr create --title "fix(server): scope classifier slug uniqueness to the organization" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

`classify_facet_unique_per_insight` was `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` — **no `organization_id`**. A classifier slug was unique across the whole install rather than within a tenant.

The three-column key was inherited verbatim from `event_classifiers` in `20260622320000` to match the extraction upsert's `ON CONFLICT` target; that table had the same omission, and nobody re-derived the key when `classify_facet` became multi-tenant.

## Why it matters

It bites **org-level** classifiers (`entity_id NULL, watcher_id NULL`) — exactly what `manage_classifiers create` produces, and the only kind `apply` and the reconciliation cron can match. The first tenant to create `sentiment` took the name from every other tenant; the second one's `create` dies on a unique violation naming a row it cannot see.

Measured on prod 2026-07-31: **29 classifiers, 3 in that globally-unique bucket across 2 orgs.** They coexist only because the slugs happen to differ — latent, not dormant.

## Red → green

Red (migration removed, test unchanged):

```
× lets two tenants each hold an org-level `sentiment`
  PostgresError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "classify_facet_unique_per_insight"
    ❯ handleCreate src/tools/admin/manage_classifiers.ts:242:34
× keeps entity-scoped slugs independent per tenant too
  PostgresError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "classify_facet_unique_per_insight"

Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
```

Green:

```
✓ src/__tests__/integration/classifiers/classifier-slug-tenancy.test.ts (4 tests)

Test Files  12 passed (12)
     Tests  36 passed (36)
```

## Notes

- The migration is strictly a **widening** — every key unique under the old constraint stays unique under the new one, so no row can conflict and no backfill is needed.
- `organization_id` is `NOT NULL` on this table (verified against prod), so adding it to the key introduces no NULL-matching subtlety. `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` is retained for the nullable `entity_id`/`watcher_id`.
- The extraction upsert's `ON CONFLICT` target moves with the constraint. Postgres resolves the column list to a specific unique index, so leaving it at three columns would fail the INSERT outright — and `classifier-slug-tenancy.test.ts` now **executes** `createClassifiersForWatcher` rather than only reading it, which is the only thing that would have caught that.
- Its `COALESCE(organization_id, EXCLUDED.organization_id)` arm is dropped as unreachable: the column is `NOT NULL` and is now itself a key column.

## Out of scope, flagged

`manage_behaviors/crud.ts:333` throws `'Authenticated user is required to create Behavior classifiers'` when `ctx.userId` is null — the same null-identity shape as #2405, but there it is a deliberate policy guard raising a clear error, not a raw constraint dump. Changing it would change auth semantics, so it is left alone.
EOF

git push -q -u origin feat/cf-model-stamp 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --title "fix(server): model-stamp classifier label vectors so a model swap can't compare across spaces" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

`classify_facet.attribute_values[value].embedding` is cosine-compared against `event_embeddings.embedding`. The **event** side is model-scoped everywhere — content search, this engine's own target fetch, the backfill's staleness predicate — because vectors from different models are not comparable even at equal dimensionality. The **label** side carried no stamp at all.

So label vectors were the half an `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` swap leaves behind. And the failure is silent: cosine between two unrelated 768-dim spaces returns a confident-looking number rather than throwing, so classification keeps emitting labels and they are simply wrong.

Measured on prod 2026-07-31: **28 classifiers, 208 label vectors, 0 stamped** — against 2,060,864 event vectors that are 100% stamped, all one model (`Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5`).

## Change

- **Writers stamp.** `hydrateAttributeEmbeddings` (create / `generate_embeddings`) and `ensureEmbedding` (the Behavior extraction path) both record the configured model. That value is *verified*, not assumed — `generateEmbeddings` already refuses a service response whose `model` disagrees with `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL`.
- **Both cosine consumers guard.** The engine drops foreign-model templates and logs a countable reason instead of a bare `No classifier templates found`; `normalizeValue` skips foreign-model values when deduping (degrading to exact string match — a spurious new value at worst, never a wrong auto-merge).
- **A stale stamp is treated as a missing embedding**, so `generate_embeddings` repairs a swap on its own rather than needing someone to remember `force_regenerate`.
- **A *missing* stamp is adopted, not discarded** — `hydrate` also runs on `create`, where the vector was just supplied by a caller on this same deployment. Discarding it would throw away input and force a needless service round-trip.
- **The backfill derives the stamp** from `event_embeddings` rather than hardcoding, so an install on a non-default model gets its own value.

## Red → green

Red (fix reverted, tests unchanged) — note the second line, which is the actual bug:

```
× stamps the configured model when create generates the vectors
  → expected undefined to be 'Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5'
× drops label vectors from a different model instead of comparing across spaces
  → expected [ 'positive' ] to deeply equal []
× treats a stale stamp as missing so generate_embeddings re-embeds it
  → expected +0 to be 1

Tests  3 failed | 1 passed (4)
```

Green:

```
Test Files  13 passed (13)
     Tests  39 passed (39)
```

## Two traps worth recording

**The obvious reproducer proves nothing.** A first draft of the drop test just flipped `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` — and passed against unfixed code, because `fetchTargetContent` scopes `event_embeddings` by model too, so the *event* vector vanishes alongside the label vector and nothing is compared at all. The test now re-embeds the event under the new model first (as the documented swap procedure does), which is the state where the cross-space cosine actually happens.

**The backfill needed its own test, and it caught a fixture bug.** The suite's migration run happens before any test data exists, so it only proves the SQL parses. `classifier-label-vector-backfill.test.ts` seeds the pre-migration shape and executes the real statement read out of the migration file. Writing it surfaced that `${JSON.stringify(v)}::jsonb` stores a jsonb **string** (double-encoded, `jsonb_typeof` = `'string'`) — the read paths parse twice and hide it, but the migration's `= 'object'` guard correctly skips such a row. The fixture now uses `sql.json` (what production uses) and asserts `jsonb_typeof = 'object'` so a mis-seeded row can never masquerade as a migration bug.

Rehearsed against prod inside a rolled-back transaction: **175 entries stamped**.

## Deploy ordering

The backfill is what keeps the new guard a no-op for data that is fine. If it did nothing, all 208 existing vectors would read as unknown-provenance and every classifier would stop classifying at deploy. Migration runs in the pre-deploy hook, so it lands first.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

input.content:
---
name: reference-embedding-model-is-a-global-env-var
description: event_embeddings supports multi-model/multi-chunk per event, but every reader pins one global EMBEDDINGS_MODEL — agents cannot generate or A/B an alternate embedding
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`event_embeddings` PK is `(event_id, embedding_model, chunk_index)` — so an event
CAN hold several vectors. The write path honors it: the worker/connector protocol
carries per-event `embedding` + `embedding_model`, and `insert-event.ts` does
delete-then-insert **scoped to the model** so two models coexist during a swap.

But the capability is unused and unreachable to agents (measured on prod 2026-07-31):

- 2,060,952 rows, **all `chunk_index = 0`**, all one model
  (`Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5`). **0 events** have more than one model.
- Every READER pins `getConfiguredEmbeddingModel()` = `process.env.EMBEDDINGS_MODEL`
  — content search, `fetchTargetContent`, `needsEmbeddingSql`, the reconciliation
  cron. A second model's vectors are therefore **write-only** until the env var
  flips process-wide.
- **No agent-facing surface exposes a model choice.** `embedding_model` appears in
  `packages/core/src/contracts/worker/protocol.ts` only — not in any tool contract
  or `sandbox/method-metadata.ts`. `manage_classifiers generate_embeddings` uses
  the server's configured model.

So the "agent generates an embedding on the fly, tests it, tunes it" loop does not
exist. Adding it means a model-scoped read parameter, not a schema change — the
storage layer is already there. See [[project_classifier_language_spike]].

description: Measured 2026-07-31 — bge mislabels Turkish negatives as positive/neutral with ZERO below-threshold warning; multilingual-e5-base scores 9/9 where bge scores 6/9
metadata:
  type: project
---

Spike run 2026-07-31 on **500 real Turkish events** from org
`8dc12bdd-5d8c-4768-a2e9-a18005cc5ebd`, against the real prod classifier
`post-sentiment` (id 201, `min_similarity` 0.5), both models via transformers.js.

| | below threshold | median cosine | hand-labelled TR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5` (current) | **0/500** | 0.585 | **6/9** |
| `Xenova/multilingual-e5-base` | **0/500** | 0.756 | **9/9** |

**The threshold gives no warning.** Both models put 0/500 below 0.5, so nothing
in the pipeline flags the failure. bge missed **every negative**, including
scoring "Rezalet, hiç memnun kalmadım" (outrageous, not satisfied at all) as
**positive**. That matches the observed prod skew on Turkish content — 186
positive / 25 negative / 289 neutral; negatives are being absorbed.

**Margin is not a usable confidence signal.** Winner-vs-runner-up median is
0.0137 for BOTH models. Discrimination lives in *which* label wins, not by how
much — so no margin-based guard would have caught this either.

Correction to an earlier claim in this session: the "220/500 below_threshold"
figure came from a prod `apply` over 500 **mixed-language** events, not a
Turkish-filtered set. It is not the baseline for this comparison.

Blocked on [[reference_embedding_model_is_a_global_env_var]] — swapping means a
2.06M-row re-embed and a global env flip; there is no way to A/B two models live.
e5 needs `"query: "` / `"passage: "` prefixes (used above).
Label vectors are now model-stamped so a swap can't silently degrade

input.content:
---
name: project-classifier-label-vector-model-stamp
description: PRs #2406 (org-scoped slug uniqueness) + #2407 (label-vector model stamp) merged 2026-07-31; prod-verify owed
metadata:
  type: project
---

Two classify_facet defects fixed 2026-07-31, both found while verifying #2402/#2405.

**#2407 `6b54e9585` — label vectors had no model stamp.**
`attribute_values[v].embedding` is cosine-compared against `event_embeddings`,
which is model-scoped everywhere. Label vectors were not, so an `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL`
swap left them behind — and cross-space cosine returns a plausible number instead
of erroring, so classification keeps emitting *wrong* labels silently. Prod had
**28 classifiers / 208 vectors / 0 stamped**. Writers now stamp; the engine drops
foreign-model templates and logs a count; `normalizeValue` skips them when
deduping; a stale stamp is treated as missing so `generate_embeddings` self-repairs.
Backfill **derives** the stamp from `event_embeddings` (prod rehearsal in a
rolled-back txn: 175 entries stamped).

**#2406 `c605b8d73` — slug uniqueness was install-wide.**
`classify_facet_unique_per_insight` was `(entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` with no
`organization_id`, inherited from `event_classifiers`. The second tenant to create
an org-level `sentiment` died on a unique violation naming an invisible row. The
extraction upsert's `ON CONFLICT` target had to move with it — Postgres resolves
the column list to a specific index, so a stale 3-column target fails the INSERT
outright. Only a test that *executes* the upsert catches that.

**Two traps worth remembering:**
- The obvious reproducer proved nothing. Just flipping `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` passes
  against unfixed code, because `fetchTargetContent` scopes events by model too —
  the event vector vanishes alongside the label vector. Must re-embed the event
  under the new model first. See [[feedback_verify_the_mutation_applied]].
- `${JSON.stringify(v)}::jsonb` stores a jsonb **string** (double-encoded,
  `jsonb_typeof='string'`). Read paths parse twice and hide it; SQL migrations do
  not. Use `sql.json`. Several existing fixtures still do the wrong thing.

**Owed:** prod-verify after rollout — confirm the 208 vectors are stamped and
classification still runs. Related: [[project_classifier_language_spike]].

content.text:
Both merged and CI-green. Rollout gate running in the background.

## First — #2402 is now prod-verified

`SELECT count(*) FROM event_classifications` against your org returned **280**, up from 0. That's the exact number I predicted, against your real data.

## Fix 4 — slug uniqueness was install-wide (#2406, `c605b8d73`)

`classify_facet_unique_per_insight` was `(entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` with no `organization_id`, inherited from `event_classifiers` and never re-derived when the table went multi-tenant. The second tenant to create an org-level `sentiment` died on a unique violation naming a row they can't see. Prod has 3 rows in that globally-unique bucket across 2 orgs — they coexist only because the slugs happen to differ.

The `ON CONFLICT` target had to move with the constraint. Postgres resolves the column list to a *specific* index, so a stale 3-column target fails the INSERT outright — the fixer caught that I'd retargeted it without ever executing it, and added a test that runs the upsert for real.

## Fix 2 — label vectors had no model stamp (#2407, `6b54e9585`)

Prod had **28 classifiers, 208 label vectors, 0 stamped**, against 2,060,864 event vectors that are 100% stamped. Writers now stamp, both cosine consumers drop foreign-model vectors, and a stale stamp counts as missing so `generate_embeddings` repairs a swap by itself. The backfill derives the model from your data rather than hardcoding.

**My first reproducer was worthless and I nearly shipped it.** Flipping `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` passes against unfixed code — `fetchTargetContent` scopes events by model too, so the event vector vanishes alongside the label vector and nothing gets compared. Re-embedding the event under the new model first produces the real red: `expected [ 'positive' ] to deeply equal []` — unfixed code emitting a confident wrong label.

## Fix 3 — the language spike, and it's worse than "less accurate"

500 real Turkish events, your actual `post-sentiment` classifier:

| | below threshold | hand-labelled Turkish |
|---|---|---|
| `bge-base-en-v1.5` (current) | **0/500** | **6/9** |
| `multilingual-e5-base` | **0/500** | **9/9** |

bge missed **every negative**, including scoring *"Rezalet, hiç memnun kalmadım"* — roughly "outrageous, not satisfied at all" — as **positive**. And `below_threshold` was 0/500, so nothing warns you. That matches your prod skew on Turkish content: 186 positive / 25 negative. The negatives aren't being missed, they're being relabelled.

Margin doesn't save you either — median winner-vs-runner-up is 0.0137 for *both* models, so no confidence guard would catch it.

One correction: the "220/500 below_threshold" I cited earlier was from a mixed-language `apply`, not a Turkish set. It wasn't the right baseline.

## Your question: multiple embeddings, agents generating on the fly

Yes on storage, no on the loop. There is a gap.

The PK is `(event_id, embedding_model, chunk_index)`, and the write path honors it — the worker/connector protocol carries per-event `embedding` + `embedding_model`, and `insert-event.ts` does delete-then-insert *scoped to the model* explicitly so two models can coexist during a swap.

But nothing uses it: **2,060,952 rows, all `chunk_index = 0`, all one model, zero events with two models.** Chunking was designed and never enabled.

The blocker is the read side. Every reader pins `getConfiguredEmbeddingModel()`, which is one process-wide env var. A second model's vectors are write-only until you flip that globally. And `embedding_model` appears in exactly one contract file — the worker protocol — and in no tool schema or SDK surface. So an agent cannot generate an alternate embedding, cannot compare two models, cannot even ask which model a vector came from.

That's why fix 3 had to run as an offline script against a local copy rather than through the product. The thing you'd want — "embed these 500 events with e5, score them, show me the diff" — has no path.

The good news: it's a read-parameter problem, not a schema migration. The storage already models exactly what you'd need.

## Confidence

- **#2402 works in prod — 97.** Ran the query against your data; got 280.
- **Both PRs correct — 90.** Real red→green on both, 39 tests, 9/9 required checks, reviews 92/92 and 90/85 with zero bugs. The migration was also rehearsed against prod in a rolled-back transaction (175 entries stamped).
- **The Turkish finding — 88.** 500 real events plus 9 hand-labelled sentences I wrote; the ground truth is small, though the failure direction is unambiguous.
- **Neither #2406 nor #2407 verified live yet — 0.** Gate is still running.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

git push -q -u origin feat/jsonb-fixture-fidelity 2>&1|tail -1; gh pr create --title "test(server): store classifier fixtures the way production does" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

The classifier fixtures bound `attribute_values` as `${JSON.stringify(v)}::jsonb`, which lands as a jsonb **string** (`jsonb_typeof = 'string'`) rather than an object — double-encoded. The read paths JSON-parse twice and hide it, so the suites passed while storing a shape production never writes.

This is not hypothetical. The identical mistake in `RunsQueue` reached prod and is documented at `runs-queue.ts:313` — it broke every `action_input ->> 'field'` reader and 403'd workers through the snapshot ownership verifier. It also cost time earlier today: it made the #2407 backfill migration look broken when the migration was correct and the fixture was not.

## The masked test

Switching to `sql.json` immediately turned one test red — and it was a test that never tested what it claimed:

```
× falls back when the best cosine is below min_similarity
  → expected 'negative' to be 'positive'
```

`falls back when the best cosine is below min_similarity` asserted `best_match_attribute === 'positive'` on an event embedded at basis 3 — **orthogonal to both attributes**, cosine exactly 0.0 each. "Closest" was a tie, decided entirely by attribute iteration order.

Under real jsonb that order is jsonb's own (key length, then bytewise — so `negative` sorts before `positive`), not authoring order. The double-encoded string preserved authoring order, so the tie happened to land on `positive` and the assertion looked meaningful.

The event vector now leans genuinely positive (cosine 0.949 vs 0.316) with both still under the 0.99 threshold, so the assertion has a real winner to name and the fallback behaviour is still what is under test.

## Guard

`seedFacet` now asserts `jsonb_typeof(attribute_values) = 'object'` after inserting, so a fixture cannot silently reintroduce the double-encoded shape.

## Scope

`agent-transcript-snapshot.test.ts` also matches the grep and is **deliberately left alone** — it reproduces the broken shape on purpose as a regression test for the RunsQueue incident.

```

```
EOF

Two classify_facet defects fixed 2026-07-31, both found while verifying #2402/#2405.

**#2407 `6b54e9585` — label vectors had no model stamp.**
`attribute_values[v].embedding` is cosine-compared against `event_embeddings`,
which is model-scoped everywhere. Label vectors were not, so an `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL`
swap left them behind — and cross-space cosine returns a plausible number instead
of erroring, so classification keeps emitting *wrong* labels silently. Prod had
**28 classifiers / 208 vectors / 0 stamped**. Writers now stamp; the engine drops
foreign-model templates and logs a count; `normalizeValue` skips them when
deduping; a stale stamp is treated as missing so `generate_embeddings` self-repairs.
Backfill **derives** the stamp from `event_embeddings` (prod rehearsal in a
rolled-back txn: 175 entries stamped).

**#2406 `c605b8d73` — slug uniqueness was install-wide.**
`classify_facet_unique_per_insight` was `(entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` with no
`organization_id`, inherited from `event_classifiers`. The second tenant to create
an org-level `sentiment` died on a unique violation naming an invisible row. The
extraction upsert's `ON CONFLICT` target had to move with it — Postgres resolves
the column list to a specific index, so a stale 3-column target fails the INSERT
outright. Only a test that *executes* the upsert catches that.

**Two traps worth remembering:**
- The obvious reproducer proved nothing. Just flipping `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` passes
  against unfixed code, because `fetchTargetContent` scopes events by model too —
  the event vector vanishes alongside the label vector. Must re-embed the event
  under the new model first. See [[feedback_verify_the_mutation_applied]].
- `${JSON.stringify(v)}::jsonb` stores a jsonb **string** (double-encoded,
  `jsonb_typeof='string'`). Read paths parse twice and hide it; SQL migrations do
  not. Use `sql.json`. Several existing fixtures still do the wrong thing.

**Owed:** prod-verify after rollout — confirm the 208 vectors are stamped and
classification still runs. Related: [[project_classifier_language_spike]].

---
name: project-bulk-classification-needs-write-time-state
description: Measured 2026-07-31 — both query-only designs for "classify everything pending" are too expensive; needs write-time materialized state
metadata:
  type: project
---

`manage_classifiers apply` requires explicit `content_ids`, max 2000, and its own
description tells the agent to "get them with a read-only SQL query first." For a
209k-event corpus that is 105 round trips carrying 2000 integers each — it also
blows out the agent's context. This is the remaining blocker on classification
being usable by a Behavior at scale.

The bulk path that already exists (`scheduled/classification-reconciliation.ts`,
`mode: 'entity'`) cannot cover it: it requires content **linked to an entity** and
classifiers **enabled on that entity**, while the content needing classification
is entity-less feed events — the same mismatch #2402 exposed.

**Both obvious query-only designs were measured on prod and both are too
expensive** (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, org `8dc12bdd-…`, LIMIT 500):

#2408 merged. Here's where everything stands.

## The main goal — verified working on your data

`6b54e9585` is live, and I ran the full loop against prod:

- **175/175** label vectors stamped, one model — the backfill did exactly what the rolled-back rehearsal predicted
- `event_classifications` still **280** — the new guard didn't drop anything real
- A live `client.classifiers.apply` over 5 events: **5/5 classified, 0 skipped**

That's define → embed → apply → read working end-to-end on your real data. Six defects deep, the classifier subsystem actually functions.

**One correction:** I wrote **208** label vectors in the #2407 commit message and PR body. The real number is **175** — I mis-added the per-classifier counts. Nothing behavioral depends on it; the migration derives its own scope and the rehearsal already said 175. But the figure in those artifacts is wrong, and it's now corrected in memory.

## Item 4 — shipped (#2408, `1f5213b3d`)

Switching the fixtures to `sql.json` immediately turned a test red, which is the whole reason it was worth doing:

```
× falls back when the best cosine is below min_similarity
  → expected 'negative' to be 'positive'
```

That test asserted `best_match_attribute === 'positive'` on an event embedded **orthogonal to both attributes** — cosine 0.0 each. It was a tie, resolved by attribute iteration order. Real jsonb orders keys its own way (length, then bytewise, so `negative` precedes `positive`); the double-encoded string preserved authoring order and made the tie look like a result. The event now leans genuinely positive (0.949 vs 0.316), both still under threshold.

`seedFacet` asserts `jsonb_typeof = 'object'` so it can't come back. Review: 93/92, zero bugs, zero slop.

## Item 3 — I'd stop, because the premise doesn't hold

"Expose model as a read parameter" doesn't get you anything on its own. To A/B e5 you need e5 vectors *for events*, and there is no agent-facing way to write those — `embedding_model` appears in exactly one contract, the worker protocol. A model override would read a vector set with zero rows in it.

The real unit of work is "evaluate a candidate model over a sample," which needs a write path too. That's a feature, not a parameter, and I don't think it's the right next thing.

## The bulk gap — I measured both designs and both are dead

`apply` needs explicit ids, max 2000. For 209k events that's 105 round trips carrying 2000 integers each. The existing bulk path (the reconciliation cron) can't help: it requires an entity link and entity-enabled classifiers, while the content is entity-less feed events — the same mismatch #2402 exposed.

I EXPLAIN ANALYZE'd the two obvious fixes on prod:

| design | time | buffers |
|---|---|---|
| anti-join on `event_classifications` | 328 ms | 261,528 |
| cursor on `ev.id` | 825 ms | 95,727 |

No index supports "(org, embedded, unclassified) ordered", and cost grows with history while the answer stays bounded — precisely the invariant against aggregating history on request paths.

So the answer is write-time materialized state (a pending marker maintained on insert, plus a backfill), not a cleverer query. That's a real design and I've deliberately **not** built it — your rule is design review before implementing, and I'd want your call on whether ambient classification is the shape you want.

## Confidence

- **#2407 correct and live — 96.** Verified against prod three ways, including a live `apply`.
- **#2408 correct — 93.** Test-only, 43/43, and it fixed a test that was asserting a coin flip.
- **#2406 not verified live — 0.** Merged and CI-green; rollout gate running.
- **Both bulk designs unviable — 90.** Real EXPLAIN ANALYZE on prod, though only on one org's data.

## Next

1. **#2406 live check** when the gate fires — two orgs can hold the same org-level slug.
2. **Decide on bulk classification.** I'd sketch the write-time pending marker for review before touching code.
3. **The e5 question stands unresolved** — Turkish negatives are being labelled positive today, with no signal. Worth deciding on its own merits, separate from the tooling gap.
4. `min_similarity: 0.5` is doing nothing for you — 0/500 below threshold on both models. Worth re-tuning regardless of which model you run.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   Two user requests in this session, both continuing a multi-session effort to make the Lobu classification subsystem genuinely usable by agents end-to-end.

   **Request 1:** "fix 4 and 2 and 3 and also tell me, if the events can have multiple embeddings, the agents can generate them on the fly test them and understand how to make them work. there is no gap in there right?"
   — Referring to my prior "Next" list: (4) `classify_facet_unique_per_insight` lacks `organization_id`; (2) stamp classifier label vectors with a model before any embedding-model swap; (3) spike `Xenova/multilingual-e5-base` on ~500 Turkish events. Plus a question about multi-embedding support and whether agents can generate/test embeddings on the fly.

   **Request 2:** "3 and 4 and also don't forget our main goal of making the behavior actually useful"
   — Referring to my newer Next list: (3) expose embedding model as a read parameter to make multi-model storage usable; (4) fix the `${JSON.stringify(v)}::jsonb` double-encoding in existing fixtures. Plus keeping focus on the overarching goal: a Behavior should be able to define → apply → read back classifications end-to-end and at scale.

   Through-line: verify every claim empirically against the real ~262k-event production corpus rather than reasoning from code.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Lobu platform**: Bun workspace monorepo; `core`/`server`/`agent-worker`/`connectors`/`embeddings`/`owletto` (submodule)
   - **Behaviors** (agent-facing name; `watcher` is internal DB vocabulary; `make pre-pr` fails on agent-facing "watcher")
   - **Classification engine**: `executeClassificationQuery({mode: 'entity'|'content_ids', organizationId, enabledClassifiers, content_ids?, entity_id?})` → returns `{content_id}[]`; cosine over `classify_facet.attribute_values[v].embedding` vs `event_embeddings.embedding`
   - **`event_embeddings` PK = `(event_id, embedding_model, chunk_index)`** — multi-model AND multi-chunk capable
   - **`getConfiguredEmbeddingModel()`** = `process.env.EMBEDDINGS_MODEL || DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL ('Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5')`; `configuredEmbeddingModelSqlLiteral()` for SQL inlining; `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS = 768`
   - **`classify_facet`**: 11 constraints (9 NOT NULL, 1 PK, 1 UNIQUE), **no FK at all**; `organization_id` is NOT NULL
   - **jsonb key ordering**: length first, then bytewise — so `negative` sorts before `positive`
   - **`sql.json()` vs `JSON.stringify(...)::jsonb`**: the latter double-encodes (jsonb_typeof = 'string')
   - **`fetch_types: false`** on the prod pool: text[] returns as raw literal `{positive}`; pgvector returns as `"[1,2,3]"`
   - **Review harness**: `REVIEWER_CLI=claude` (codex quota-blocked until Aug 5); `make review-fix` before first `make review`
   - **Rollout gate**: `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` — merge commit FIRST

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **PR #2406 (merged `c605b8d733490833c2f641590109b92ce527690b`), worktree `cf-org-unique`:**

   - **`db/migrations/20260731140000_classify_facet_org_scoped_unique.sql`** (NEW):
     ```sql
     -- squawk-ignore disallowed-unique-constraint,prefer-robust-stmts,constraint-missing-not-valid -- config-scale table (29 rows on prod); brief lock acceptable; dbmate wraps in a transaction
     ALTER TABLE classify_facet DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS classify_facet_unique_per_insight;
     ALTER TABLE classify_facet ADD CONSTRAINT classify_facet_unique_per_insight
         UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (organization_id, entity_id, watcher_id, slug);
     ```
     Down-migration comment: "Narrowing, so this aborts if two tenants have since taken the same slug — correctly."

   - **`packages/server/src/watchers/classifier-extraction.ts`**:
     ```ts
     options: {
       createdBy: string;
       // Required, not `string | null`. It is part of the ON CONFLICT key below,
       // and `classify_facet.organization_id` is NOT NULL — so the old
       // `organizationId ?? null` could only ever produce a 23502...
       organizationId: string;
     },
     ```
     and the conflict target (comment explains Postgres resolves ON CONFLICT to a specific index):
     ```sql
     ON CONFLICT (organization_id, entity_id, watcher_id, slug) DO UPDATE
     SET name = EXCLUDED.name,
         updated_at = NOW()
     ```
     (dropped `organization_id = COALESCE(classify_facet.organization_id, EXCLUDED.organization_id)` as unreachable)

   - **`packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/classifiers/classifier-slug-tenancy.test.ts`** (NEW, 4 tests incl. one added by the fixer that executes `createClassifiersForWatcher`)

   **PR #2407 (merged `6b54e9585ff0434590959a6b0143ae49ae5536ac`), worktree `cf-model-stamp`:**

   - **`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_classifiers.ts`** — `hydrateAttributeEmbeddings`, final form:
     ```ts
     const isForeignModel =
       config.embedding_model != null && config.embedding_model !== configuredModel;
     const reusable = hasEmbedding && !isForeignModel;
     if (!reusable || options.forceRegenerate) {
       valuesToEmbed.push(value);
     }
     updated[value] = {
       description: config.description,
       examples: config.examples,
       embedding: reusable ? (config.embedding as number[]) : undefined,
       embedding_model: reusable ? configuredModel : undefined,
     };
     ```
     and on generation: `updated[value] = { ...updated[value], embedding: embeddings[index], embedding_model: configuredModel };`

   - **`packages/server/src/utils/classification-query.ts`** — added `import { configuredEmbeddingModelSqlLiteral, getConfiguredEmbeddingModel } from './embeddings';`, plus in `fetchClassifierTemplates`:
     ```ts
     const configuredModel = getConfiguredEmbeddingModel();
     let staleTemplates = 0;
     ...
     if (attrObj.embedding_model !== configuredModel) {
       staleTemplates++;
       continue;
     }
     ...
     if (staleTemplates > 0) {
       logger.warn({ staleTemplates, usableTemplates: templates.length, configuredModel, classifiers: enabledClassifiers },
         '[Classification Query] Dropped label vectors embedded by a different model — run manage_classifiers generate_embeddings to re-embed them under the configured model');
     }
     ```

   - **`packages/server/src/watchers/classifier-extraction.ts`** — added `embedding_model?: string | null` to `AttributeValue`; `ensureEmbedding` stamps `getConfiguredEmbeddingModel()` on worker vectors and clears both on absence; `normalizeValue` skips foreign-model entries:
     ```ts
     const configuredModel = getConfiguredEmbeddingModel();
     for (const [existing, config] of Object.entries(existingValues)) {
       if (!hasValidEmbedding(config.embedding)) continue;
       if (config.embedding_model !== configuredModel) continue;
       const similarity = cosineSimilarity(newEmbedding, config.embedding);
     ```

   - **`db/migrations/20260731150000_classify_facet_label_vector_model_stamp.sql`** (NEW) — derives the stamp:
     ```sql
     WITH prevailing AS (
         SELECT COALESCE(
             (SELECT embedding_model FROM public.event_embeddings
               GROUP BY embedding_model ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1),
             'Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5') AS model
     )
     UPDATE public.classify_facet cf
     SET attribute_values = (
             SELECT jsonb_object_agg(e.key,
                 CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(e.value) = 'object'
                  AND jsonb_typeof(e.value -> 'embedding') = 'array'
     ```

---
name: project-bulk-classification-needs-write-time-state
description: "Measured 2026-07-31 — both query-only designs for \"classify everything pending\" are too expensive; needs write-time materialized state"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 13f0fe8f-d0cb-4f1a-b19c-1621ef6e6b2b
  modified: 2026-07-31T16:35:56.628Z
---

`manage_classifiers apply` requires explicit `content_ids`, max 2000, and its own
description tells the agent to "get them with a read-only SQL query first." For a
209k-event corpus that is 105 round trips carrying 2000 integers each — it also
blows out the agent's context. This is the remaining blocker on classification
being usable by a Behavior at scale.

The bulk path that already exists (`scheduled/classification-reconciliation.ts`,
`mode: 'entity'`) cannot cover it: it requires content **linked to an entity** and
classifiers **enabled on that entity**, while the content needing classification
is entity-less feed events — the same mismatch #2402 exposed.

**Both obvious query-only designs were measured on prod and both are too
expensive** (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, org `8dc12bdd-…`, LIMIT 500):

| design | time | buffers |
|---|---|---|
| anti-join `NOT EXISTS event_classifications` + embedding `EXISTS` | 328 ms | 261,528 |
| cursor `ev.id > $n` + embedding `EXISTS` | 825 ms | 95,727 |

There is no index supporting "(org, embedded, unclassified) ordered", and cost
grows with history while the answer stays bounded — exactly the
"request paths never aggregate history" invariant.

**Verdict: needs write-time materialized state** (a pending marker/counter
maintained on insert), per that same invariant, plus a backfill migration. Do NOT
ship a cleverer query. Design first — do not implement unprompted, see
[[feedback_design_review_before_implementing]].

Note: exposing an embedding-model read parameter does NOT enable model A/B on its
own — there is no agent-facing way to WRITE event vectors under an alternate
model, so a model override would read an empty vector set. See
[[reference_embedding_model_is_a_global_env_var]] and
[[project_classifier_language_spike]].

---
name: project-classifier-label-vector-model-stamp
description: "PRs #2406 (org-scoped slug uniqueness) + #2407 (label-vector model stamp) merged 2026-07-31; prod-verify owed"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 13f0fe8f-d0cb-4f1a-b19c-1621ef6e6b2b
  modified: 2026-07-31T16:35:42.028Z
---

Two classify_facet defects fixed 2026-07-31, both found while verifying #2402/#2405.

**#2407 `6b54e9585` — label vectors had no model stamp.**
`attribute_values[v].embedding` is cosine-compared against `event_embeddings`,
which is model-scoped everywhere. Label vectors were not, so an `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL`
swap left them behind — and cross-space cosine returns a plausible number instead
of erroring, so classification keeps emitting *wrong* labels silently. Prod had
**28 classifiers / 175 vectors / 0 stamped** (the "208" in the #2407 commit
message and PR body is a mis-addition of the per-classifier counts — the correct
figure is 175, confirmed by both the rehearsal and the live backfill).
Writers now stamp; the engine drops
foreign-model templates and logs a count; `normalizeValue` skips them when
deduping; a stale stamp is treated as missing so `generate_embeddings` self-repairs.
Backfill **derives** the stamp from `event_embeddings` (prod rehearsal in a
rolled-back txn: 175 entries stamped).

**#2406 `c605b8d73` — slug uniqueness was install-wide.**
`classify_facet_unique_per_insight` was `(entity_id, watcher_id, slug)` with no
`organization_id`, inherited from `event_classifiers`. The second tenant to create
an org-level `sentiment` died on a unique violation naming an invisible row. The
extraction upsert's `ON CONFLICT` target had to move with it — Postgres resolves
the column list to a specific index, so a stale 3-column target fails the INSERT
outright. Only a test that *executes* the upsert catches that.

**Two traps worth remembering:**
- The obvious reproducer proved nothing. Just flipping `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` passes
  against unfixed code, because `fetchTargetContent` scopes events by model too —
  the event vector vanishes alongside the label vector. Must re-embed the event
  under the new model first. See [[feedback_verify_the_mutation_applied]].
- `${JSON.stringify(v)}::jsonb` stores a jsonb **string** (double-encoded,
  `jsonb_typeof='string'`). Read paths parse twice and hide it; SQL migrations do
  not. Use `sql.json`. Several existing fixtures still do the wrong thing.

**PROD-VERIFIED 2026-07-31** on revision `6b54e9585`: 175/175 label vectors
stamped, one distinct model; `event_classifications` still 280; and a live
`client.classifiers.apply` over 5 events returned **5/5 classified, 0 skipped**.
That is the full loop working on real data — define → embed → apply → read.

Related: [[project_classifier_language_spike]],
[[reference_embedding_model_is_a_global_env_var]].

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

<!-- Project rules for agents (Claude, pi, codex). CLAUDE.md inlines this into every session — keep this file lean. Put package-specific detail in the nearest package AGENTS.md. -->

## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.
